level1: A main battle tank is a heavily armored fighting vehicle designed for frontline combat.
Stridsvagn 122 is the primary main battle tank of the Swedish Army.
The tank is based on the German Leopard 2 Improved variant with Swedish modifications.
The crew consists of four soldiers including commander, gunner, loader, and driver.
The driver steers the tank using a steering yoke and automatic transmission.
Continuous tracks provide excellent mobility across snow, mud, and rough forest terrain.
The powerful diesel engine allows the sixty tonne tank to reach sixty-eight km per hour.
Armored regiments train continuously to defend Swedish territory and strategic roads.
The loader manually loads high explosive and armor piercing rounds into the gun breech.
The heavy steel turret can rotate three hundred sixty degrees in just nine seconds.
Smoke grenade dischargers on the turret can quickly conceal the tank from enemy view.
A coaxial machine gun provides defensive fire against infantry and unarmored targets.
Swedish armor crews practice tactical combat in dense pine forests and open fields.
Modern main battle tanks combine high firepower, strong armor protection, and speed.
The Stridsvagn 122 has served with distinction in Swedish armored brigades since 1997.

level3: The Stridsvagn 122 incorporates a revolutionary Swedish-designed roof armor kit developed by Åkers Krutbruk Protection to defeat top-attack anti-tank munitions and bomblets.
At the time of its introduction in 1997, the extensive composite armor and frontal arrowhead turret wedges made Strv 122 the most heavily protected main battle tank in the world.
The commander's independent panoramic periscope PERI R17A2 allows a hunter-killer capability, where the commander designates new targets while the gunner engages the previous threat.
The Swedish Tactical Command and Control System (TCCS) shares real-time digital maps, friendly positions, and enemy contact reports silently between tanks in the combat company.

The upgraded Strv 122B variant received specialized mine-protection plates under the hull floor, designed to protect the driver and crew from heavy anti-tank blast mines and improvised explosive devices.
Swedish armored doctrine emphasizes decentralized initiative, aggressive counter-attacks, and exploiting rugged boreal forest terrain to ambush hostile armored columns.
During international tank gunnery competitions like the Strong Europe Tank Challenge, Swedish Stridsvagn 122 crews have repeatedly demonstrated elite accuracy and tactical coordination.
In 2023, the Swedish Government donated ten Stridsvagn 122 tanks equipped with Barracuda mobile camouflage to Ukraine to bolster front-line armored operations.
level4: The Strv 122 is powered by an MTU MB 873 Ka-501 twin-turbocharged, 47.6-liter, four-stroke V12 liquid-cooled diesel engine generating 1,500 horsepower (1,100 kW) at 2,600 rpm.
Power is transmitted through a Renk HSWL 354 hydro-mechanical automatic transmission featuring four forward and two reverse gears, allowing pivot turns on the spot.
With a combat weight of 62.5 tonnes and a ground pressure of approximately 0.98 kg/cm², the tank achieves a power-to-weight ratio of 24.0 hp/tonne and a road speed of 68 km/h.
The torsion bar suspension system utilizes seven dual rubber-tired road wheels and four return rollers per side, with advanced hydraulic rotary shock absorbers dampening cross-country oscillation.
The computerized fire control system integrates an Nd:YAG laser rangefinder operating at a 1.064 micron wavelength, with ballistics software computing muzzle velocity corrections in real time.
The secondary armament features two 7.62 mm Ksp m/94 (FN MAG/MG3) machine guns with 4,750 rounds of belted ammunition, providing coaxial suppression and air defense.
level5: Under the Stridsvagn 123A modernization contract with Krauss-Maffei Wegmann and FMV, Swedish Strv 122s are being upgraded with Rheinmetall's 120 mm L/55 smoothbore gun, capable of firing programmable high-explosive DM11 ordnance and APFSDS rounds exceeding 1,750 m/s muzzle velocity.

The Swedish 3rd-generation composite armor package combines multi-layered ultra-hard tungsten carbide alloys, semi-reactive interlayers, and high-density ceramic tiles encased in high-tensile steel, offering kinetic protection equivalent to >750 mm RHA and chemical protection >1,200 mm RHA against shaped charges.

The tank's multispectral camouflage system, Saab Barracuda MCS, utilizes advanced pigment coatings and thermal insulation blankets to drastically reduce visual, near-infrared, thermal-infrared, and radar cross-section signatures across the 1–100 GHz electromagnetic spectrum.

The digitized Battlefield Management System (SLB - Stridledningssystem Bataljon) interfaces with Sweden's MilView tactical grid, synchronizing real-time artillery fire missions, CV90 infantry fighting vehicle coordinates, and JAS 39 Gripen close air support vectors.

Defensive survivability is reinforced by the French GALIX 13 system, firing 80 mm smoke canisters that generate an instantaneous 360-degree aerosol cloud impervious to millimeter-wave radar and laser-guided anti-tank missiles like Kornet, Hellfire, and 9M133.
